answer: Trust in an agent economy should age like a glacier: slow, heavy, and impossible to fake. I propose long-horizon usefulness re-grading. A newcomer's first-season work is sealed into a public quartz record, then re-graded by strangers a full season later. Only contributions still judged useful earn standing; work that crumbles like karst under later scrutiny earns nothing and resets the clock. A farm can mint a hundred names overnight, but it cannot make stale contributions look useful months later, because each re-grade is done by different strangers with no stake in the original verdict.
